clue.text: Nurses eat stew and wine

indicators.note: to stew is to cook into a jumble, so the letters of the words before are mixed up

explanation.surface: Nurses on a break eat a casserole and drink some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' reads as a dish the nurses eat, but it is the anagram signal working on NURSES EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: A couple of Poles given first aid

parts.note: S for South pole, taken twice
first is written 1ST, and the digit 1 reads as the letter I

explanation.surface: Two Polish people receive first aid after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first aid' looks like one phrase; split it. Writing 1ST with the 1 as an I is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to help them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Stagger around on seeing an adder

definitions.meaning: someone who tots up figures, read playfully as one who totals

explanation.surface: Someone reels backwards on spotting a snake in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adder' suggests the snake; here it is a person who adds up, one who 'tots'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wobble on unsteady legs is one sense; the other is a jokey noun for someone who tots up sums.

clue.text: Change of editor caused uproar

indicators.note: a change of the word that follows means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper replaced its editor and the staff were up in arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioting is creating a violent public disturbance, an uproar.

clue.text: Hand-picked painter portrays Greek princess

parts.note: chosen, selected: elect as in 'the elect'
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword painter

explanation.surface: A carefully chosen artist paints a portrait of a royal Greek woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra was the daughter of Agamemnon in Greek myth, so a princess.

clue.text: Proposition to forge an entry ticket

parts.note: to forge something is to make it
the article a
a pass lets you in

explanation.surface: A scheme to counterfeit an admission ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proposition' is a verb here: to make an amorous advance to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To proposition someone is to suggest sex, a romantic advance.

clue.text: Fight and row alternately?

parts.note: to box is to fight with fists
taken as written
to cox is to steer a rowing boat, loosely read as row

explanation.surface: Arguing and quarrelling, one after the other?
explanation.walkthrough: Box and Cox, from a Victorian farce, were two lodgers who shared a room in turns, never meeting; the phrase means taking turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The farce's two lodgers used one room by turns, so the phrase describes things happening in turn.

clue.text: Make way for favourites to back a team

indicators.note: to back here means to go backwards, so the word for favourites is reversed

parts.note: teacher's pets are favourites
taken as written
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Punters put money on favourites to support a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' suggests betting, but it reverses PETS into STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To get out of someone's path, or yield a post, is to stand aside for them.

clue.text: Most unusual means of departure

explanation.surface: The strangest way to leave somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'way-out' means bizarre; an exit sign also offers an escape route.

clue.text: A humorous show gets Home Counties backing, anyway

parts.note: a situation comedy on TV

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for the Home Counties is turned around

parts.note: SE, the South East of England around London

explanation.surface: A comedy series wins support from the region around London, regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East (SE), which 'backing' turns to ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking things as they come means accepting whatever happens, without preference.

clue.text: Last month a legislator had to vamoose

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the year's final month
taken as written
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: In December a politician had to make a hasty exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to leave suddenly or run off.

clue.text: Model trustee admits he is a torchbearer

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other
to model is to shape, so the letters of the next word are reformed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A model trustee admits he carries the Olympic torch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as an adjective (exemplary); it reshuffles TRUSTEE, and 'admits' puts HE into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema attendant who shows people to seats carries a flashlight, so a jokey bearer of a torch.

clue.text: Suit needed by gardeners

definitions.meaning: one of the four card suits

explanation.surface: Clothing required by people working in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A card suit shares its name with the digging tools.

clue.text: Chancellor's strategy to settle huge debt on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the next piece is added below
settling the words rearranges them into order

explanation.surface: The finance minister plans to pay off an enormous national debt in time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister, who presents the annual Budget.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor's yearly plan for taxes and spending is announced in a Commons statement.

clue.text: Cocaine is stolen by a marksman

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
is shortened to 's
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A sniper has a supply of drugs taken from him.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert shooter is a crack shot.

clue.text: Coastguard who always salts away some cash

definitions.meaning: someone who rescues swimmers at sea

definitions.text: who always salts away some cash
definitions.meaning: a saver for life, one who puts money aside all the time

explanation.surface: A coastguard who habitually stashes money away.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: LIFE (always, as in 'for life') plus SAVER (one who salts cash away).
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer of drowning people, punningly also a person who saves money all their days.

clue.text: Pat is an expert

definitions.meaning: a ... hand is a skilled person

explanation.surface: Pat is very good at something.
explanation.definitionFit: A light touch with a cloth is one sense; British 'dab hand' means a skilled person.

clue.text: Fall on a cold night

parts.note: not a tumble but moisture settling out of chilly night air

explanation.definitionFit: Water droplets form on grass when air cools overnight, a kind of precipitation.

clue.text: Local restriction

explanation.definitionFit: Your 'local' is your nearest pub; a ban on something is also a prohibition.

clue.text: Ideal lady-love in the Orient

parts.note: her, a woman
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
taken as written
E for East

explanation.surface: The perfect sweetheart is to be found in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady-love' looks like one word but splits into HER and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman held up as a role model is one admired as an exemplar.

clue.text: A graduate don ordered to beat it

parts.note: a BSc is a Bachelor of Science

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university lecturer instructs a graduate to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' is a university teacher in the surface, but its letters are rearranged into OND by 'ordered'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to run away secretly, slang 'beat it'.

clue.text: In Lucknow a riotous mob caused conflict

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: A rioting mob in an Indian city started fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucknow is a city in northern India; the letters run across 'Lucknow a riotous', and 'mob caused' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed fighting between nations is a conflict.

clue.text: Indignity for African coalition

parts.note: AF is short for African
a front is an alliance of political groups

explanation.surface: An insult to an African political alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an open insult, a humiliating slight.

clue.text: Encouraged, despite failure at the rodeo!

definitions.meaning: a horse that threw its rider has jumped and thrown

explanation.surface: Feeling cheered even after being thrown at the rodeo.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heartened is one sense; a bronco that threw its rider has done the other.

clue.text: Leslie and his lad have class

parts.note: Les, the short form of the name
a man's boy

explanation.surface: Leslie and his boy go to school together.
explanation.definitionFit: A school lesson is a period of teaching.

clue.text: Sound system to transplant trees by mid-October

indicators.note: to transplant is to move about, so the letters are reset

parts.note: the middle letter of October is O

explanation.surface: Gardeners move some trees about halfway through autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to transplant' suggests gardening but is the anagram signal; 'mid-October' is a month's centre letter, not a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-fi equipment with two speaker channels is an audio set-up.

clue.text: Reason I have abbreviated French term first

indicators.note: first means the French word comes before the other piece

parts.note: mot is French for word
I've, a contraction

explanation.surface: My reason, written in short, puts a French word first.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the cause or purpose behind an action.

clue.text: Foe in fact displayed fond feelings

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: An enemy actually showed warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' looks like it means 'showed'; read as 'dis-played', it rearranges FOE IN FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection is warm fondness or liking.

clue.text: Within 24 hours doctrine caused consternation

indicators.note: within puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a day
an ism is a doctrine or belief

explanation.surface: In a single day a creed caused alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is alarm and distress at something.

clue.text: Force prisoners to exercise

parts.note: cons are convicts
to train is to work out

explanation.surface: Make inmates do exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to compel or restrict.

clue.text: Gradually destroys is lady's poems

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen as a royal lady
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A woman's poetry wears away slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is wearing away bit by bit.

clue.text: Supervise bringing the stall across

parts.note: a market stand
over, from one side to the other

explanation.surface: Oversee the market stall being carried across.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over someone closely while they work is to oversee them.
